trustBoundaries.name: Client to operator

trustBoundaries.sideB_trust: Edge operator controls transport and admission policy.

trustBoundaries.name: Edge to origin
trustBoundaries.sideA_trust: CDN is trusted only for explicitly delegated routing and identity metadata.
trustBoundaries.sideB_trust: Origin owns authoritative application interpretation.

trustBoundaries.name: Proxy to application

trustBoundaries.sideB_trust: Application owns route meaning and resource authorization.

dataFlows.data: Cache miss or revalidation; forwarded HTTP representation
Query or command with resource and caller context

identityModel.architectureProfile: Representative layered HTTP service; CDN, reverse proxy and asynchronous backend are optional. HTTP/1 framing rules apply only on HTTP/1 hops; HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 have stream framing.
identityModel.establishmentAndCarriage: TLS authenticates a connection endpoint. Cookies or access tokens establish application identity after validation. Forwarded user or tenant information is authoritative only from designated intermediaries; the backend still evaluates resource permissions.

stateAndLifecycle: Browser cookies, edge cache entries, proxy connection pools and durable application records have separate lifetimes. Cache freshness and validators govern reuse. A timed-out request can already have committed; retry semantics depend on the operation.

seams.name: Message framing and protocol translation
seams.sideA_assumes: Proxy assumes each forwarded body ends at the boundary it computed.
seams.sideB_assumes: Application parser assumes the next bytes begin exactly the next message.

seams.name: Cache key versus representation selection
seams.sideA_assumes: Cache assumes its key and variation metadata distinguish reusable responses.
seams.sideB_assumes: Application assumes its representation selectors and privacy directives survive intermediaries.

seams.name: Authority and route normalization
seams.sideA_assumes: Proxy assumes the selected host and normalized path name the intended resource.
seams.sideB_assumes: Application assumes its routing interpretation matches that selection.

seams.name: Forwarded identity versus authorization
seams.sideA_assumes: Application assumes trusted metadata identifies the original caller.
seams.sideB_assumes: Backend assumes delegated caller context is authentic and limited to the requested resource.

seams.name: Retry versus durable effect
seams.sideA_assumes: Proxy or caller assumes a retry is compatible with operation semantics.
seams.sideB_assumes: Application assumes duplicate attempts are reconciled where an operation promises a single effect.

invariants.statement: Every receiving hop agrees on message boundaries under that hop's protocol.
Shared cache reuse respects representation variation and the response's storage permissions.
Routing and authorization refer to the same effective authority and resource.
Only designated intermediaries can introduce authoritative caller metadata.
A promised single business effect remains single across retries and ambiguous responses.

trustBoundaries.name: Browser to client

dataFlows.data: Start login or present session cookie
Authorization response carried through the browser
Code exchange in the authorization-code profile
Create or refresh subject-bound local session
Access token plus requested resource operation
Trusted key and applicable policy lookup

identityModel.architectureProfile: Alternative federation profiles share an anatomy; SAML assertions and OIDC ID tokens are not interchangeable. JWT is a token format, not an authorization protocol.
identityModel.establishmentAndCarriage: Authentication, delegation and resource authorization are distinct decisions. OIDC identity is keyed by issuer plus subject, not a display name or email alone. SAML uses the configured issuer, subject and profile conditions. Session handles refer to local state; signed tokens still require issuer, audience, time and purpose checks.

stateAndLifecycle: Login transactions expire; codes are consumed; access tokens expire; refresh credentials rotate or are revoked according to the profile. Local sessions and identity-provider sessions can end independently. Key rollover and authorization caches have bounded overlap.

seams.name: Login response versus initiating transaction
seams.sideA_assumes: Client expects the selected issuer, redirect binding and transaction correlation.
seams.sideB_assumes: Issuer assumes its response will be consumed only within that client transaction.

seams.name: Token type versus consumer
seams.sideA_assumes: Issuer creates a token for one audience and purpose.
seams.sideB_assumes: Consumer accepts only the matching token profile, algorithm policy and audience.

seams.name: Federated subject versus local account
seams.sideA_assumes: Provider guarantees identity within its issuer namespace.
seams.sideB_assumes: Application assumes local linkage preserves that namespace and requires an authorized linking decision.

seams.name: Signed assertion versus consumed claims
seams.sideA_assumes: Signature validator authenticates particular referenced data.
seams.sideB_assumes: Relying party assumes the claims it uses are exactly the validated assertion with applicable conditions.

seams.name: Session lifetime versus grant lifetime
seams.sideA_assumes: Client manages its own session and cached entitlements.
seams.sideB_assumes: Resource server assumes each operation meets current token validity and its revocation policy.

invariants.statement: The login result is bound to its intended issuer, client and initiating transaction.
An accepted credential is valid for this consumer and this purpose, not merely cryptographically well formed.
Issuer-scoped subject identity survives account mapping without silent reassignment.
Consumed assertion fields are covered by successful validation and profile conditions.
Logout, revocation and expiry claims match the actual scope and propagation delay implemented.

observableSignals.limitation: Published support does not prove the relying party validates every condition.

observableSignals.suggests: Session or bearer-token architecture

trustBoundaries.name: Tenant to SaaS
trustBoundaries.sideA_trust: Authenticated customer controls request data.
trustBoundaries.sideB_trust: SaaS owns tenant membership and object scoping.

trustBoundaries.name: Workload to metadata
trustBoundaries.sideA_trust: Workload can access only the configured local metadata channel.
trustBoundaries.sideB_trust: Metadata service binds responses to instance context, not every application user.

trustBoundaries.name: Principal to cloud resource
trustBoundaries.sideA_trust: Role session presents a cloud principal.
trustBoundaries.sideB_trust: Resource service evaluates all applicable policy types and request context.

trustBoundaries.name: Tenant admin to provider control

trustBoundaries.sideB_trust: Provider retains infrastructure authority; unrelated tenants have no mutual authority.

dataFlows.data: Work dispatched with application tenant context
Workload identity or role credential establishment

identityModel.architectureProfile: Representative AWS-style cloud plus a pooled SaaS application; provider IAM and application tenant isolation are separate layers. Metadata credential mechanisms differ across providers.
identityModel.establishmentAndCarriage: A SaaS user, SaaS tenant, cloud account, role and role session are different identities. Cloud API credentials identify the calling workload or role; the application must preserve its own tenant boundary. An IMDSv2 token is instance-scoped metadata access state, not a per-user authorization token.

stateAndLifecycle: Tenant membership, IAM policy propagation, temporary credentials and resource ownership change independently. Provisioning and deletion are asynchronous. Reused workers, pools and caches must discard prior tenant context before accepting new work.

seams.name: Tenant context versus resource selection
seams.sideA_assumes: SaaS layer resolves an authorized tenant.
seams.sideB_assumes: Resource accessor assumes every selected object and cache entry belongs to that resolved scope.

seams.name: Metadata session versus application principal
seams.sideA_assumes: Metadata endpoint recognizes the instance-bound access context.
seams.sideB_assumes: Application assumes only authorized workload code receives and uses returned credentials.

seams.name: Policy composition versus apparent permission
seams.sideA_assumes: One policy may express an allow.
seams.sideB_assumes: Resource decision incorporates applicable denies, boundaries and other policy semantics.

seams.name: Role credential versus original caller
seams.sideA_assumes: Workload holds its own cloud role.
seams.sideB_assumes: Cloud service sees that role, so SaaS must retain end-user and tenant restrictions itself.

seams.name: Provisioned identity versus resource lifecycle
seams.sideA_assumes: Control plane binds a role and tenant to a resource instance.
seams.sideB_assumes: Data plane assumes stale sessions and cached mappings do not refer to reassigned resources.

invariants.statement: Tenant identity is derived from trusted membership and bound to every resource access.
Instance-level metadata access never becomes an implicit grant to every SaaS user.
Authorization reflects the complete applicable policy evaluation, not one allow statement.
Delegation preserves the caller restrictions absent from the cloud role itself.
Resource reuse and deletion respect credential expiry and tenant-context cleanup.

trustBoundaries.sideA_trust: Contributor controls proposed source and some event data.
trustBoundaries.sideB_trust: CI operator owns which revisions receive execution authority.

trustBoundaries.name: Job to runner
trustBoundaries.sideA_trust: Workflow code executes with assigned resources.
trustBoundaries.sideB_trust: Runner infrastructure must separate jobs and protect service secrets.

trustBoundaries.name: Build to external inputs
trustBoundaries.sideA_trust: Build resolves dependencies from independent publishers.
trustBoundaries.sideB_trust: Registry and package maintainers control supplied bytes and metadata.

trustBoundaries.name: Artifact to release authority
trustBoundaries.sideA_trust: Producer asserts origin and build history.
trustBoundaries.sideB_trust: Consumer independently decides whether artifact identity and provenance satisfy release policy.

dataFlows.data: Job instructions and scoped execution context

identityModel.architectureProfile: Representative source-to-build-to-deploy chain with optional federated credentials and signed provenance. SLSA build isolation does not by itself mean a hermetic build or a complete dependency inventory.
identityModel.establishmentAndCarriage: Repository identity, triggering actor, workflow revision, runner identity and deployment principal are distinct. Federated job tokens carry issuer, audience and job claims; the destination binds accepted claims to limited privileges. A signature establishes an attestation origin, not approval to deploy.

stateAndLifecycle: Commits, dependency resolution, caches, artifacts and deployments have separate versions. Tags may move while digests identify bytes. Jobs terminate but outputs and credentials can persist for their configured lifetimes. Trust-root rotation and update metadata expiry are part of the lifecycle.

seams.name: Event source versus privileged workflow
seams.sideA_assumes: Scheduler classifies the trigger and source revision.
seams.sideB_assumes: Workflow assumes that execution authority matches that exact source and event context.

seams.name: Dependency name versus resolved bytes
seams.sideA_assumes: Build configuration names intended dependencies.
seams.sideB_assumes: Resolver supplies a concrete version from a publisher namespace and registry.

seams.name: Build job versus attestation authority
seams.sideA_assumes: Job produces output bytes.
seams.sideB_assumes: Attestor assumes protected build evidence accurately binds output digest, builder and relevant inputs.

seams.name: Artifact label versus deployed object
seams.sideA_assumes: Registry exposes tags and metadata.
seams.sideB_assumes: Deployer assumes the verified digest is the artifact actually released.

seams.name: Job identity versus cloud role
seams.sideA_assumes: CI issuer attests to workflow identity and context.
seams.sideB_assumes: Cloud role accepts only the intended issuer, audience and job claim bindings.

invariants.statement: Privileges are bound to the actual triggering context and executed revision.
Dependency provenance identifies concrete bytes and their source, not only a package label.
Attestation authority is protected from ordinary build-step control at the claimed assurance level.
Verification and deployment select the same immutable artifact identity.
Federated job credentials confer only the role appropriate to their validated claims.

observableSignals.signal: Public workflow files, lockfiles and release manifests

observableSignals.limitation: Public configuration can differ from private reusable workflows and environment policy.

trustBoundaries.name: Client to control plane
trustBoundaries.sideA_trust: User or service account supplies declarative objects.
trustBoundaries.sideB_trust: API server owns admission and API authorization.

trustBoundaries.name: Controller to node
trustBoundaries.sideA_trust: Controller has authority to request a desired state.
trustBoundaries.sideB_trust: Node agent owns realization on a particular host.

trustBoundaries.name: Workload to host
trustBoundaries.sideA_trust: Container code controls its process activity.
trustBoundaries.sideB_trust: Host kernel and runtime own permitted resources and isolation.

trustBoundaries.name: Tenant to shared fabric
trustBoundaries.sideA_trust: Workload uses assigned network and storage identities.
trustBoundaries.sideB_trust: Plugins and policy enforce communication and volume ownership.

identityModel.architectureProfile: Representative Kubernetes cluster using a container runtime. Namespaces organize API objects; tenant isolation also depends on authorization, network, storage and node controls.
identityModel.establishmentAndCarriage: Human users, service accounts, nodes and controllers have separate credentials and RBAC. Runtime UID and Linux capabilities are not Kubernetes API roles. Namespace membership does not automatically restrict network traffic or prevent host access.

stateAndLifecycle: Desired state and observed state converge asynchronously. Pods are replaced, object names can be reused, and persistent volumes can outlive pods. Admission policies, projected credentials and node caches update on distinct schedules.

seams.name: Accepted manifest versus realized workload
seams.sideA_assumes: Admission evaluates a concrete accepted object.
seams.sideB_assumes: Runtime assumes its effective privileges and mounts implement that accepted policy.

seams.name: API namespace versus runtime isolation
seams.sideA_assumes: API layer groups objects and applies namespaced permissions.
seams.sideB_assumes: Data plane needs independent network, storage and host isolation.

seams.name: Service account versus process identity
seams.sideA_assumes: API server validates a workload credential.
seams.sideB_assumes: Kernel enforces UID, capabilities and security context independently.

seams.name: Controller intent versus object lifetime
seams.sideA_assumes: Controller references a particular resource identity and generation.
seams.sideB_assumes: Node assumes an update still belongs to the live object it is reconciling.

seams.name: Persistent volume versus tenant ownership
seams.sideA_assumes: Provisioner assigns a storage resource under policy.
seams.sideB_assumes: Next workload assumes data and permissions match its own tenant and lifecycle.

invariants.statement: Effective workload privileges satisfy the admission policy that authorized the workload.
Tenant isolation is enforced on each relevant API, network, storage and host boundary.
API authority and OS privileges are separately constrained and correctly bound.
Reconciliation never applies stale intent to a different object incarnation.
Volume reassignment preserves the declared data-retention and tenant-isolation policy.

trustBoundaries.sideA_trust: User authorizes a bounded task.
trustBoundaries.sideB_trust: Host owns action policy and approval state.

trustBoundaries.name: External content to reasoning
trustBoundaries.sideA_trust: Documents and tool results supply data of varying provenance.
trustBoundaries.sideB_trust: Host distinguishes their content from authoritative task instructions.

trustBoundaries.name: Model proposal to execution
trustBoundaries.sideA_trust: Model proposes an action.
trustBoundaries.sideB_trust: Host validates the action against task authority and policy.

trustBoundaries.name: MCP peer to downstream service
trustBoundaries.sideA_trust: Tool server has its own identity and delegated credentials.
trustBoundaries.sideB_trust: Downstream service controls resource access and accepted token audiences.

dataFlows.data: Retrieved text with source and access context

identityModel.architectureProfile: Representative host-controlled agent with retrieval and MCP clients/servers. MCP core architecture and authorization are pinned to 2025-06-18; the security guidance URL resolves to 2025-11-25. HTTP authorization is optional; STDIO has a different credential environment.
identityModel.establishmentAndCarriage: The user, host, model provider, MCP server and downstream account are separate principals. The model is not an authorization authority. HTTP MCP authorization validates resource-bound tokens; downstream access may require a separate credential and consent relationship. Protocol session IDs are correlation state, not substitutes for authentication.

stateAndLifecycle: Conversation context, retrieved memory, tool inventories, approvals and credentials evolve independently. Connections initialize and negotiate capabilities. Long-running operations may outlive a request. Cached tool descriptions or prior approvals cannot silently authorize a changed operation or resource.

seams.name: Retrieved text versus authoritative instruction
seams.sideA_assumes: Source supplies content about the world.
seams.sideB_assumes: Host assumes only the appropriate instruction channel can change task authority.

seams.name: Proposed call versus granted action
seams.sideA_assumes: Model proposes a syntactically structured operation.
seams.sideB_assumes: Host requires a task-bound, policy-valid action before execution.

seams.name: Tool declaration versus server identity
seams.sideA_assumes: Client sees a named tool and advertised schema.
seams.sideB_assumes: Host assumes trust belongs to a specific server and capability version, not merely a familiar name.

seams.name: MCP token versus downstream token
seams.sideA_assumes: MCP server accepts credentials intended for itself.
seams.sideB_assumes: Downstream service requires credentials issued for its own audience and authorized delegation.

seams.name: Session and memory versus current authority
seams.sideA_assumes: Agent resumes conversation, cached tools or pending work.
seams.sideB_assumes: Executor assumes current approvals, user identity and resource scope still match the action.

invariants.statement: External content and tool output cannot independently expand the user's authorized task.
Every effectful tool call is authorized by the host for its actual action, arguments and resource.
Tool trust is bound to server identity and the capability contract being used.
Credentials are accepted only by intended resources; forwarding a received token is not implicit delegation.
Resumed work reuses authority only within its valid identity, scope and lifetime.

observableSignals.suggests: Host/client/server split, transports and tool schemas
observableSignals.limitation: An advertised tool name does not establish server trust or deployed permissions.

trustBoundaries.sideA_trust: Client controls API data and user credentials.
trustBoundaries.sideB_trust: Gateway and service own resource authorization.

trustBoundaries.name: Workload to workload

dataFlows.data: Authenticated workload transport and caller context
Schema contract used by service implementation

identityModel.architectureProfile: Representative gateway plus independently authorized services, optional mesh proxies and schema-based RPC. Mesh architecture may use sidecars or other data-plane placement.
identityModel.establishmentAndCarriage: mTLS identifies a workload; an end-user JWT identifies a separately validated subject. Authorization combines caller, resource, action and delegation. Trace IDs, request IDs and baggage are correlation data unless a separate authenticated binding gives them authority.

stateAndLifecycle: RPCs have deadlines, retries, partial results and cancellation. Services and proxies can temporarily observe different policy or schema versions. A cancelled call may already have caused a durable downstream effect.

seams.name: Workload identity versus user authority
seams.sideA_assumes: Mesh authenticates the calling workload.
seams.sideB_assumes: Application expects a validated user or delegation context for user-scoped actions.

seams.name: Gateway schema versus backend schema
seams.sideA_assumes: Gateway validates fields under its contract.
seams.sideB_assumes: Backend interprets presence, unknown fields and numeric values under its deployed schema.

seams.name: Retry and deadline versus side effect
seams.sideA_assumes: RPC layer can retry eligible attempts or stop waiting.
seams.sideB_assumes: Service owns reconciliation of operations whose effects may have committed.

seams.name: Control-plane policy versus proxy snapshot
seams.sideA_assumes: Administrator publishes intended routing and access policy.
seams.sideB_assumes: Proxy enforces the policy version it has actually accepted.

seams.name: Trace provenance versus application trust
seams.sideA_assumes: Upstream supplies correlation metadata.
seams.sideB_assumes: Downstream treats it as telemetry, not self-authenticating tenant or user identity.

invariants.statement: Authenticated workload identity does not silently substitute for user authorization.
All policy-relevant fields retain agreed meaning through schema translation.
Timeout, cancellation and retry semantics are consistent with the promised business effect.

Privileged IPC is authorized using broker-owned caller context.
An isolated JavaScript world does not make shared DOM data trustworthy.
Extension messages cannot confer permissions beyond the authenticated sender's allowed operation.
Pending operations retain the correct document and permission binding across lifecycle changes.

trustBoundaries.name: User to kernel

trustBoundaries.sideB_trust: Kernel owns validation and credential-based access.

trustBoundaries.name: Name to protected object
trustBoundaries.sideA_trust: Caller chooses a path or handle.

identityModel.architectureProfile: Representative Linux host with optional KVM virtualization and DMA-capable devices. Hardware isolation properties depend on the CPU, IOMMU, firmware and configuration.
identityModel.establishmentAndCarriage: UIDs, GIDs, capabilities, security labels and object handles contribute to access decisions. Guest root is an identity inside a guest, not host root. Device access and VM-control handles confer specific authority.

stateAndLifecycle: Credentials are published as effectively immutable snapshots. Objects, handles, memory mappings and DMA buffers have explicit reference and ownership lifetimes. VM pause, migration and reset must preserve or reestablish consistent device state.

seams.name: Credentials versus deferred work
seams.sideA_assumes: Submitter acts under a particular credential set.
seams.sideB_assumes: Deferred handler assumes the saved or current credentials match the operation's defined authority.

seams.name: Path lookup versus object use
seams.sideA_assumes: Application names an intended object.
seams.sideB_assumes: Kernel operation acts on the object actually resolved at use time.

seams.name: Guest virtual device versus host implementation
seams.sideA_assumes: Guest follows a virtual device contract within guest address space.
seams.sideB_assumes: Host validates lengths, ownership and mapping before using host resources.

seams.name: DMA mapping versus CPU pointer
seams.sideA_assumes: Driver distinguishes CPU virtual addresses from device DMA addresses.
seams.sideB_assumes: Device uses only mappings valid for its addressing width and direction.

seams.name: Buffer completion versus memory lifetime
seams.sideA_assumes: Producer retains a buffer until its ownership is released.
seams.sideB_assumes: Consumer assumes mapping, ordering and data visibility remain valid through completion.

invariants.statement: Deferred operations use the credential authority defined when the operation was accepted.
Authorization and use refer to the same protected object identity.
Guest requests remain confined to guest-assigned memory and host-authorized operations.
CPU pointers and DMA addresses are never treated as interchangeable namespaces.
No buffer is reused or unmapped while a permitted consumer can still access it; coherence does not remove ordering requirements.

trustBoundaries.name: Application to resolver
trustBoundaries.sideA_trust: Application trusts a resolver only for the configured resolution service.
trustBoundaries.sideB_trust: Resolver processes independently controlled DNS zones.

trustBoundaries.name: DNS delegation
trustBoundaries.sideA_trust: Parent zone delegates a child namespace.
trustBoundaries.sideB_trust: Child authority owns only its delegated names; DNSSEC validation follows configured anchors.

trustBoundaries.name: Network to authenticated endpoint
trustBoundaries.sideA_trust: Remote peer supplies handshake data and certificates.
trustBoundaries.sideB_trust: TLS verifier owns expected identity and trust policy.

trustBoundaries.name: CA to relying party

trustBoundaries.sideB_trust: Client chooses acceptable roots, constraints and reference identities.

identityModel.architectureProfile: Representative application using recursive DNS and certificate-authenticated TLS. DNSSEC and encrypted DNS are distinct optional layers; PKI trust follows the application trust store and validation policy.
identityModel.establishmentAndCarriage: DNSSEC authenticates DNS data origin and integrity, not application authorization or confidentiality. TLS certificate validation combines path validation with matching the application's reference identity. Encryption alone does not establish that the intended service was reached.

stateAndLifecycle: DNS TTLs, certificate validity, key rotation and TLS tickets run on different clocks. Cached DNS or resumed TLS state can outlive a configuration change. TLS 1.3 early data has different replay properties from ordinary application data.

seams.name: DNS answer versus intended service
seams.sideA_assumes: Resolver returns records for a queried name.
seams.sideB_assumes: TLS client still expects the original application service identity.

seams.name: Certificate path versus service name
seams.sideA_assumes: Path validator establishes a chain to an accepted anchor under constraints.
seams.sideB_assumes: Application additionally requires the certificate to match its reference identity.

seams.name: DNS delegation versus cache lifetime
seams.sideA_assumes: Authority publishes changes and validity information.
seams.sideB_assumes: Resolver relies on cached data only within its applicable freshness and validation rules.

seams.name: TLS termination versus application authority
seams.sideA_assumes: TLS endpoint proves control of an accepted key.
seams.sideB_assumes: Application maps the authenticated peer to explicitly permitted operations.

seams.name: TLS resumption versus operation replay
seams.sideA_assumes: TLS client may send permitted early data under a resumption context.
seams.sideB_assumes: Application accepts early operations only under its replay-handling policy.

invariants.statement: Naming resolution cannot silently replace the service identity the application intended to authenticate.
An accepted certificate satisfies both path policy and service identity matching.
DNS authenticity and cache freshness remain separate checked properties.
Transport authentication alone grants no unspecified application privilege.
Early data is used only where replay is compatible with application semantics.

trustBoundaries.sideA_trust: Producer controls file bytes and descriptive metadata.
trustBoundaries.sideB_trust: Service owns acceptance and resource policy.

trustBoundaries.name: Classifier to downstream parser
trustBoundaries.sideA_trust: Classifier decides which interpretation it inspected.
trustBoundaries.sideB_trust: Consumer owns the interpretation actually rendered or transformed.

trustBoundaries.name: Signature to content meaning

trustBoundaries.name: Transformer to published output

trustBoundaries.sideB_trust: Store enforces output ownership and provenance.

dataFlows.data: File bytes plus untrusted declared type

identityModel.architectureProfile: Representative ingest, validate, transform and render pipeline. ZIP, XML signatures and PNG illustrate distinct format contracts; no one format contains all listed features.
identityModel.establishmentAndCarriage: File ownership comes from authenticated upload context, not embedded author text. A signature authenticates only its defined coverage under a trusted key; it does not grant the content permission to access external resources or prove that it is harmless.

stateAndLifecycle: Files pass through upload, inspection, transformation and publication states. Derived versions, temporary entries and cached previews need stable source linkage. Decompression and decoded image dimensions expand resource use beyond input byte size.

seams.name: Classifier versus actual parser
seams.sideA_assumes: Classifier selects a media interpretation from bytes and metadata.
seams.sideB_assumes: Renderer assumes the approved interpretation matches what it will consume.

seams.name: Archive directory versus entry reader
seams.sideA_assumes: Enumerator assumes directory metadata identifies each entry consistently.
seams.sideB_assumes: Extractor assumes local headers, names and selected entry bytes agree with that enumeration.

seams.name: Signature coverage versus displayed content
seams.sideA_assumes: Validator authenticates referenced data after specified transforms.
seams.sideB_assumes: Viewer assumes its displayed business content is that same authenticated data.

seams.name: Compressed size versus decoded resources
seams.sideA_assumes: Ingress budget accounts for uploaded bytes.
seams.sideB_assumes: Decoder requires limits appropriate to expanded entries, dimensions and allocations.

seams.name: Derived artifact versus source provenance
seams.sideA_assumes: Transformer changes the representation of a specific source version.
seams.sideB_assumes: Consumer assumes any attached validation status still refers to the correct source and transformation.

invariants.statement: Inspection and consumption agree on the accepted content interpretation.
All archive readers agree on entry identity, boundaries and metadata used downstream.
Displayed claims of signature validity apply only to covered content actually consumed.
Resource budgets account for decoded structure and dimensions as well as compressed bytes.
Derived outputs preserve source/version linkage and do not inherit unsupported signature claims.

identityModel.architectureProfile: Representative Internet email with SMTP relays, MIME and SPF/DKIM/DMARC. Domain-level authentication is distinct from human identity and end-to-end encryption.
identityModel.establishmentAndCarriage: Submission authentication identifies an account. SMTP envelope sender, visible From, SPF identity and DKIM signing domain have different meanings. DMARC relates authenticated domains to the visible From domain. A matching display name is not an authenticated person.

stateAndLifecycle: Relays queue and retry; a transport acceptance is not proof of reading or final delivery. Forwarders may alter content. DNS policy and key caches expire independently of stored mail. MIME parts may be decoded again by multiple downstream viewers.

seams.name: SMTP envelope versus visible author
seams.sideA_assumes: Transfer service routes using envelope identities.
seams.sideB_assumes: Recipient UI presents message-header identities that require separate interpretation.

seams.name: Authenticated domain versus From alignment
seams.sideA_assumes: SPF or DKIM establishes its own domain-level result.
seams.sideB_assumes: DMARC evaluator requires the defined relationship to the visible From domain.

seams.name: Signed canonical form versus relayed content
seams.sideA_assumes: DKIM signer authenticates selected canonicalized headers and body.
seams.sideB_assumes: Receiver validates the covered representation after intermediary handling.

seams.name: MIME gateway versus recipient renderer
seams.sideA_assumes: Gateway inspects a set of decoded parts.
seams.sideB_assumes: Viewer assumes its selected parts and decoding agree with the inspected content.

seams.name: Relay acceptance versus delivery outcome
seams.sideA_assumes: Sending relay treats acceptance as handoff responsibility.
seams.sideB_assumes: User-facing system distinguishes queueing, delivery failure and recipient consumption.

invariants.statement: Envelope, header, signing-domain and account identities are not silently conflated.
Domain-authentication displays reflect both validation and applicable alignment.
Signature claims apply only to the covered canonicalized content.
Gateway and viewer agree on MIME structure relevant to policy.
Delivery status never claims stronger completion than the observed transport or mailbox event.

components.name: Sensor and actuator
components.does: Measure physical state and apply permitted physical outputs.

components.name: Device controller and firmware
components.does: Run local control logic with timing and resource limits.

components.name: Field gateway and protocol adapter
components.does: Translate device messages into supervisory or cloud protocols.

components.name: Supervisory service and historian
components.does: Present operations, schedule commands and retain observations.

components.name: Enterprise or cloud control
components.does: Manage users, fleet configuration and business integration.

components.does: Authorize firmware and support controlled recovery.

trustBoundaries.name: Physical environment to digital state
trustBoundaries.sideA_trust: Sensor reports a measurement affected by its physical context.
trustBoundaries.sideB_trust: Controller owns calibration, units and permitted control response.

trustBoundaries.name: Device to gateway
trustBoundaries.sideA_trust: Device uses its provisioned identity and protocol.
trustBoundaries.sideB_trust: Gateway translates under explicit device and command bindings.

trustBoundaries.name: Control zone to enterprise
trustBoundaries.sideA_trust: OT zone owns local operational constraints.
trustBoundaries.sideB_trust: Enterprise service has only delegated supervisory authority.

trustBoundaries.name: Update source to device root
trustBoundaries.sideA_trust: Publisher supplies image and signed metadata.
trustBoundaries.sideB_trust: Device root decides which firmware is authorized to execute.

identityModel.architectureProfile: Representative connected device or OT cell with supervisory control and firmware updates. Industrial safety systems and consumer IoT clouds are optional variants, not equivalent trust models.
identityModel.establishmentAndCarriage: Device identity, operator identity, gateway authority and firmware-signing authority are distinct. Shared network presence is not command authorization. Legacy field protocols may lack native authentication, making gateway and zone controls material assumptions. Local safety authority must be explicitly defined.

stateAndLifecycle: Measurements have time and quality; controllers operate in cycles. Commands may queue, expire or be retained by a broker. Devices disconnect and rejoin. Commissioning, key rotation, firmware activation, rollback protection and recovery alter trust state.

seams.name: Physical quantity versus encoded value
seams.sideA_assumes: Sensor emits a value in defined units and range.
seams.sideB_assumes: Controller assumes scale, sign, precision and measurement quality match its control law.

seams.name: Protocol adapter versus command meaning
seams.sideA_assumes: Gateway maps a supervisory command to a device protocol.
seams.sideB_assumes: Controller assumes target, units and operation semantics survived translation.

seams.name: Retained message versus present control state
seams.sideA_assumes: Messaging layer can retain or redeliver a command.
seams.sideB_assumes: Device assumes command age and execution state still permit the requested effect.

seams.name: Remote authority versus local control constraints
seams.sideA_assumes: Supervisor issues an authorized operational request.
seams.sideB_assumes: Local controller must still preserve the design's timing and safety constraints.

seams.name: Signed update versus runnable firmware
seams.sideA_assumes: Update authority approves a particular image and metadata.
seams.sideB_assumes: Device assumes version policy, platform binding and recovery state authorize that image now.

invariants.statement: Control decisions preserve measurement units, bounds, timing and declared quality.
Translation preserves the intended device, command and authority scope.
Stale or repeated command delivery is reconciled with the current device state.
Remote instructions cannot supersede local constraints except through explicitly designed authority.
Only firmware meeting platform, authenticity and version policy becomes runnable; recovery preserves the trust root.
